items.text: No adult-use (recreational) cannabis. Possessing any cannabis without a 329 registration is a petty misdemeanour, except 3 g or less, which is a violation with a US$130 fine.

Medical cannabis needs a Hawaii 329 card. International visitors can't use the out-of-state route; they must be certified by a Hawaii medical provider and apply as in-state patients. The Department of Health advises against travelling with cannabis.

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Travel pono (responsibly). Don't take rocks, sand, plants or wildlife. Never touch or stand on coral; use mineral-based reef-safe sunscreen.
culture-and-protocol.sacred_or_restricted_places: At heiau and other wahi pana (storied places), stay on designated paths and obey kapu (keep-out) signs. Keep quiet. Don't sit, stand, walk or lean on dry-stacked stone walls, and don't move, add or stack rocks or leave physical offerings.

sites.name: Puʻu o Mahuka Heiau
sites.era: possibly built in the 1600s, enclosures added probably in the 1700s; in use until 1819
sites.what: Largest heiau on Oʻahu, almost 2 acres of walled stone enclosures above Waimea Valley. The park page reports signal fires linking it with the heiau at Wailua on Kauaʻi, and notes suggestions that three of Vancouver's men killed in 1792 were taken here.
